newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore May non-oil exports seen at 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore May non-oil exports seen at 3.5 pct.

text.p: Singapore's non-oil exports for May were likely be 3.5 percent higher year-on-year, a Reuters poll of economists revealed on Thursday.

Confirmation of the figure on Friday, when the government is likely to announce it, would confirms the uptrend for exports and that the economy was on track for fuller recovery in the second half of the year.
Another sign of stronger growth down the road was a parallel rise in industrial output, which rose 1.1 percent year-on-year in April after five consecutive months of falls.
Credit growth, also on the mend, was further evidence that manufacturing and exports were improving, economists said.
The same Reuter poll produced an average forecast of 1.9 percent in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for May year-on-year, unchanged against the rate in April.

The Singapore dollar has remained flat, which discounts the impact of exchange rates on imports, some economists said, but local cost pressures from transportation and domestic fees were creeping into the index.
Singapore's Trade Development Board is expected to publish its official export data for April at 0400 GMT on June 20.
